Excommunicate

ex-kuh-MYOO-nih-kayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To excommunicate to formally expel someone from a religious community.

The medieval church would excommunicate any noble who refused to pay the required tithes.

Worked Example

The council threatened to excommunicate the monk after he publicly challenged the pope's authority.

Excommunicate is a formal, official term specifically for a religious body cutting someone off from membership and its rites.

Antonyms

ordain

welcome

welcome: receive someone warmly into a group

How Strong Is It? — reprimand → excommunicate → anathematize

reprimand vs. excommunicate

reprimand vs. excommunicate: A reprimand is a formal scolding, but it doesn't remove someone from the group.

anathematize vs. excommunicate

anathematize vs. excommunicate: To anathematize someone is to formally curse and condemn them, an even more severe religious punishment than excommunication alone.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of excommunicate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: out of (Latin)

Root — commun

Root — commun: common, shared (from Latin communis, 'common, shared')

Suffix — -icate

Suffix — -icate: to make, to cause (Latin -icare + -ate, the same ending as in communicate)

Put it together

Put it together: ex- ("out of") + commun ("shared," from Latin communis) + -icate ("to make") = to put someone out of the shared community.

Use the root in a new word: community

Use the root in a new word: community: The same root gives us "community," the everyday word for a group of people who share something in common -- exactly what excommunication removes someone from.

Word Choice

Excommunicate is specifically a religious term for formal expulsion from a church or faith community, unlike Ostracize, which describes any group's informal social exclusion of someone.
